text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The five-nation ceasefire monitoring group ruled that Israel was responsible for shelling a south Lebanon village on Sunday.
-Judicial authorities charged seven people, including four Lebanese, with illegally shipping 680 tonnes of toxic plastic waste from Germany to Beirut.
-One Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militiaman wounded in guerrilla attack in south Lebanon.
-The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanese commercial banks stood at $21.4 billion in Sep 1996.
-Political sources say forming the new cabinet may be postponed until Sunday if it is not formed today.
-Christian Maronite Patriarch Sfeir, before heading to the Vatican, says: "We demand our friends to help us in regaining our sovereignty."
-U.S. ambassador to Lebanon Richard Jones says: "I do not expect an escalation in south Lebanon."
-Gas stations postponed a one-day strike planned for today to next week.
-Saudi envoy hands a message to President Hrawi from Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz.
-Government revenues from taxation of property deals rose by nearly a third in the first 10 months of this year.
